findings.title: No task specifies how the local head sha for the "behind" check is obtained
findings.description: Task 6.1 defines `check_head_pushed(host, locator, *, head: str, local_sha: str, cwd: str)` — `local_sha` arrives as a caller-supplied parameter. Task 3 adds only `current_branch` and `commits_in_range`; neither yields the working tree's HEAD sha. Task 13.1's wiring order ("resolve locator → preconditions (identity, then pushed) → …") never names obtaining `git rev-parse HEAD`, and no other task owns it. The success criterion "a branch whose host sha differs from local fails … with the same command" is unit-tested with a sha passed in (Task 6.2), but the production producer of that value is unspecified. A junior AI would likely infer `git rev-parse HEAD`, but under the project's no-inferred-values discipline this should be an explicit step — either a helper in Task 3 alongside `current_branch`, or a named sub-step of Task 13.1.

findings.title: `PrInputs` and the combined `gather_inputs` have no owning task
findings.description: Task 7.1 says to create `inputs.py` with "the commit and slice halves of `gather_inputs`", and Task 8.1 adds `find_latest_in_range_review(...)` to the same file — but neither task creates the `PrInputs` dataclass that Task 9.1's `assemble_facts(inputs: PrInputs)` consumes, nor completes `gather_inputs` by combining the three halves, nor tests their combination. Each half is tested in isolation (7.2, 8.2), so the assembled input object and its contract (what fields exist, how absence is represented) are left to be invented at Task 9. This is the seam between Tasks 7/8 and Task 9 and should be an explicit step in Task 7.1 or a small follow-on.

findings.title: The review's `verdict` is carried into assembly but never read by the scan task
findings.description: Task 8.1 specifies reading only `reviewedSha` from frontmatter, while Task 9.1's `PrFacts` carries "its verdict" and Task 11.1 writes "the artifact path, verdict, and reviewed sha" under review provenance. Reading the `verdict` field from the already-selected file's frontmatter is an easy inference (the success criterion explicitly requires the verdict on the page), but no checklist line states it. Worth one added bullet in Task 8.1.
